task: Diagnose the Workers/DO outbound-audio stall
what_held: the stall is REAL: 11 stalls in 25 runs of one identical configuration (arm=after, parkMode=main, durableHistory on), each ~9.2-10.0s against a 10s park, i.e. audio held for almost exactly the park duration. Too precisely correlated with the park to be network congestion.

Same code, same config, same client. Because of that clustering, the two diagnosis experiments are VOID: (a) concurrent park -> 3/3 clean, (b) durableHistory off -> 3/3 clean, but the POSITIVE CONTROL (durableHistory back on, parking handler, identical build) also came back 3/3 clean. With a control that does not reproduce, neither clean result carries information.
claim_retracted: I previously reported this as located -- 'audio produced and dispatched but not flushed, leading candidate DO output gating'. The localization half still stands (see below); the attribution to a specific trigger does NOT, and the earlier report implied more certainty than the data supports.
what_survives: during stalls the bus kept dispatching tts.audio at rates indistinguishable from clean runs (stalled 26-102 dispatches during the park; clean 56-103 -- overlapping). So audio was produced, dispatched to handlers, and handed to a synchronous socket.send(), yet not delivered. The hold is in egress, below the bus. That part is unchanged.
methodological_lesson: arms were run in SEPARATE SEQUENTIAL BATCHES, so each arm saw different platform conditions. Against a temporally clustered fault that design cannot distinguish the arm from the epoch. Any retry must interleave arms within one batch, or find an on-demand reproducer first.

task: Diagnose the Workers/DO outbound-audio stall
root_cause: an awaiting NON-concurrent bus handler defers delivery of INBOUND provider-socket events on Workers/DO, so TTS audio stops being produced for the duration of the await and resumes when it releases. The media lane cannot help: it routes audio that has already arrived, and here the audio never arrives. Consistent with Cloudflare's documented input-gate rule -- events are deferred until the object 'is no longer executing JavaScript code'.
claim_corrected: the earlier report said audio was 'produced and dispatched but not flushed', i.e. held EGRESS, inferred from a COUNT of tts.audio dispatches during the park. That inference was invalid -- a count cannot separate 'spread through the park' from 'stopped early'. Timestamping settles it: last dispatch offsets were 342, 1775, 1994, 1848, 1821, 3703ms into a 10000ms park with ZERO dispatches in the final 500ms. Dispatch stops early every run; held egress would keep dispatching for the whole park.
why_it_looked_intermittent: the client-visible gap is the REMAINDER of the park after production stopped. A run only shows a gap if the utterance was still going when the park ended; a short utterance finishes inside the park and reads clean. That is the ~40% incidence, not a flaky platform.
microbench: built a provider-free microbench (worker-media-lane-microbench.ts + run-media-lane-microbench.ts) with arms INTERLEAVED inside one batch, fixing the sequential-batch flaw that voided the earlier attempts. 220 trials, ZERO stalls across raw DO socket, agents-SDK Connection, confirmed and unconfirmed storage probes, and concurrent-vs-parked handlers. It does not reproduce because its frames come from a LOCAL TIMER rather than an inbound socket event -- and that non-reproduction is what localizes the fault to event delivery.
hypotheses_killed: (1) DO OUTPUT GATING -- predicted an un-awaited storage.put() before the park would stall every run; it stalled 2/5. Refuted by a failed deterministic prediction, and consistent with the input-gate rule explicitly exempting storage completion events. (2) drain-loop starvation -- mediaResolver and restResolver are separate. (3) agents-SDK Connection.send -- 20 interleaved trials, zero stalls.
prior_art_checked: gh cloudflare/workerd and cloudflare/agents: no matching issue. cloudflare/agents#1991 is await-sensitive send loss but is facet/RPC-bridge specific and not our path. Cloudflare's input/output gate semantics came from the 'Durable Objects: Easy, Fast, Correct' blog post, which is what made the mechanism nameable.
